clue.text: Vulgar relations have finished going on stage

indicators.note: the second piece is placed on top of the first, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
when things have finished they are over

explanation.surface: Actors whose crude affairs ended once they went on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for an act of sex, so crude 'relations' in the carnal sense.

clue.text: Disreputable, extremely short, wasn't standing up straight

indicators.note: short at both extremes, so the first and last letters are cut off

parts.note: someone who slumped instead of standing tall slouched

explanation.surface: A shady character, very short and with poor posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely short' looks like a description of height; it trims both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche describes someone shady or of dubious morals, not respectable.

clue.text: Gee! Douglas' cat is bad-tempered

parts.note: gee is the spoken name of the letter G
Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, home of the tailless Manx cat, of which a rumpy is the fully tailless type

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone called Douglas whose cat is cranky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Douglas' looks like a person's name; it is the Manx capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy person is irritable and sulky.

clue.text: Loved piece about early mode of transport

indicators.note: about here means round and about, so the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A cherished part of an old vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an early bicycle or tricycle from the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Not completely straight with lawyers about minister

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so bar is read backwards

parts.note: the bar is the body of barristers
someone bisexual is not entirely heterosexual

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is somewhat dishonest with his lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straight' looks like 'honest'; it means heterosexual.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious leader and teacher, a minister of a congregation.

clue.text: Piercing whistle — ref's blowing up too much

indicators.note: the scrambled ref goes through the middle of the other piece, piercing it

parts.note: rhyming slang: 'whistle and flute' means suit

indicators.note: a thing blowing up is blasted apart, so the letters of ref are rearranged

explanation.surface: A referee blasts a shrill whistle far more than necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' scrambles REF and 'Piercing' sets the result inside the suit. Cockney rhyming slang shortens 'whistle and flute' (meaning suit) to 'whistle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, an oversupply beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Possible replacement's in box — leave lid off

parts.note: to spar is to box

indicators.note: the lid of a down word is its top letter, here taken off

parts.note: to leave is to depart

explanation.surface: A spare item is sitting in a box, so remove its lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare component is kept in case one wears out and must be swapped.

clue.text: One side with money abroad

parts.note: right is one side, abbreviated R
with means and, together with

explanation.surface: One faction backed by cash from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The rand is South Africa's currency, so foreign cash to a British solver.

clue.text: Sense crew's keeping OK

indicators.note: the crew holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
OK as assent means yes

explanation.surface: A boat crew retains its good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sense' looks like common sense; it is one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, the faculty of seeing.

clue.text: When you do this, stop people drinking too much

parts.note: read as instructions, the answer says throw the word pots about, and its letters fall into the word stop

explanation.surface: Advice to boozers: once you start doing this, call a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer's first half is an anagram signal acting on its second, making the clue's 'stop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term of abuse for drunkards, people who habitually drink to excess.

clue.text: Start to undress in land by middle of Wimbledon Common

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: the USA is a land, a country

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of undress
Wimbledon has nine letters, so its middle is the fifth

explanation.surface: Someone begins stripping off on Wimbledon Common, a park in south-west London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside USA. 'Wimbledon Common' reads as one place name; the definition is the final word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Common as an adjective means ordinary or customary, the normal run of things.

clue.text: Admitting home's completely out of cups — that's stupid!

indicators.note: the first piece lets the second in, holding it inside

parts.note: cups are a bra's, so having none at all is going bra-less
at home means in

explanation.surface: Someone notices the house has run out of teacups and calls it idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' looks like crockery; it is the cups of a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no brain is foolish, so the word means dim-witted.

clue.text: Actors cast ready at last — hopes to include brief review

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take the review inside them
cast in the sense of thrown about, so the letters are rearranged
at last points to the final letter of ready

parts.note: crit is short for critique, a review

explanation.surface: A cast of actors, ready at last, hope a short review will mention them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the company of actors but is the anagram signal on Y and HOPES, giving HYPOES; 'to include' then takes in the short review.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek the word meant a stage player; today it names people who pretend, playing a role.

clue.text: Piece of straw is perhaps thus described

definitions.text: Piece of straw is perhaps thus described

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small fragment of straw might be given a particular name.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'thus described' names nothing; the definition is the whole clue, 'Piece of straw', with 'Piece of' also signalling the letters inside 'straw is perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin tuft or strand of straw or hair is called by this name.

clue.text: A night in with back occasionally massaged? That'll never happen!

indicators.note: massaged means kneaded, so the letters are worked into a new order
occasionally picks every other letter of back, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for an evening at home with a back rub, and is told no chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' gives A and K from back; 'massaged' reworks them with A NIGHT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to reconsider is a scornful refusal, saying their expectation is hopeless.

clue.text: Drive's big — what may follow?

parts.note: a drive leading up to a house is its approach; the 's is kept as S
big in the sense of popular or in demand, which is hot

explanation.surface: A golfer hits a huge tee shot and wonders what comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like golf, and the definition plays on that: after the tee drive comes the stroke onto the green. In the wordplay it is a driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, the stroke played towards the green usually comes after the drive off the tee.

clue.text: Staggered round city — time to be taken back into house

indicators.note: the staggering piece goes round the others, holding them inside

parts.note: to reel is to stagger
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone lurched round town and was then readmitted to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is the House of Commons, Britain's elected chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP voted back into parliament at a further election has been returned for another term.

clue.text: Feature of golfing Masters — one embraced in another sport

indicators.note: the swing piece wraps round the others, holding them inside

parts.note: the swing is a central part of a golf stroke
one is the Roman numeral I
M is the abbreviation for master, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Something characteristic of the Masters golf tournament turns up inside a different sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masters' looks like the Augusta golf tournament; it is MM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool or open-water race is a sport distinct from golf, so 'another' fits.

clue.text: Prince getting worried talked rubbish

parts.note: someone rattled is unnerved or worried

explanation.surface: A rattled royal babbled nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter idly or foolishly at length is to babble nonsense.

clue.text: Big deal, right? Won't work — like government's contact-tracing app

indicators.note: the letters are worked over, kneaded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A sarcastic dismissal of the UK government's much-hyped Covid contact-tracing app, which failed.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson promised a 'world-beating' tracing app in 2020; it was abandoned. 'work' looks like part of 'won't work' but shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministers boasted their tracing system would be best on the planet, which is the phrase's sense.

clue.text: Direction to players — Desdemona extremely upset, Iago devious

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top
extremely points to the letters at the very extremes of Desdemona
devious means winding off course, so the letters of Iago are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stage directions for Othello: Desdemona greatly distressed, Iago scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' looks like actors in Othello; they are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian tempo marking tells musicians to play slowly.

clue.text: One bloody woman initially kissed trainspotter

parts.note: one is the article a
'Bloody Nora!' is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of kissed

explanation.surface: A woman kissed a train enthusiast first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for an obsessive fan of an unglamorous hobby.

clue.text: That man's failing, mate — but he's still in office

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the letters of that man fall apart into a new order

parts.note: cock is old British slang for a friend, as in 'wotcha, cock'

explanation.surface: A complaint that a useless politician somehow keeps his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' reads as a noun, a fault; it is the anagram signal on THAT MAN. Written in 2020, when the health secretary was criticised over Covid but stayed in post.
explanation.definitionFit: When the puzzle appeared he was the UK Health Secretary, a minister still holding his cabinet post.

clue.text: Rosemary here? Gig's beginning in where she normally drinks at lodge

indicators.note: in here says the G from Gig goes inside the words for her usual bar

parts.note: a woman's local pub would be her bar

indicators.note: the beginning of Gig is its opening letter

parts.note: a lodge is an animal's home, as a den is

explanation.surface: A woman named Rosemary turns up at a gig in her usual bar at a lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosemary' poses as a woman's name; it is the herb, and the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a culinary plant typically grown in a plot of kitchen plants.

clue.text: Crucial point about children in pack

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the nub is the central point of a matter

explanation.surface: A key issue regarding children in a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunch is a group or gang of people, as a pack is.

clue.text: Angry when London statue's toppled

indicators.note: toppled in a down clue means knocked over, read bottom to top

parts.note: Eros is the statue at Piccadilly Circus in London

explanation.surface: Someone is furious after a monument in London is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue at Piccadilly Circus is popularly called Eros.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore is informal for annoyed or resentful.

clue.text: Maybe illegal? Vlad intends to not get involved

parts.note: the setter Vlad saying 'I will' would write I'll

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of not get are rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter refuses to get mixed up in something possibly unlawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods obtained dishonestly or unlawfully are acquired by bad means, so possibly criminal.

clue.text: A cycling expert's forecast

indicators.note: cycling sends a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a guru is an expert or master

explanation.surface: A cycling pundit makes a prediction about a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the last U of GURU to the front, giving UGUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to predict or portend, as Roman priests read omens.

clue.text: Spurs wanting a final point getting a stroke of luck

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the A is dropped

parts.note: to spur is to goad, so spurs are goads
the end is the final point

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspurs, missing a last goal, get lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; here it is a plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something welcome that arrives unexpectedly, as if sent from heaven, is a piece of good fortune.
